claims.statement: The Azure guide covers FPT/GHEC/GHES and describes token federation through azure/login; GHES requires self-hosted runners.
OIDC prerequisites require at least one trust condition excluding untrusted repositories. Dependabot dynamic event_name is feature-gated to FPT/GHEC/GHES>3.20; GHE.com substitutions are GHEC-only.

The Azure guide says repositories created after July15,2026 and repositories renamed/transferred after that date use immutable owner/repository-ID subjects; existing repositories keep the prior format unless opted in, and GHES is excluded. Preserve this guide-specific wording.
For GHES Azure must reach discovery/JWKS endpoints and the JWT issuer must be publicly routable; Entra ID has no fixed IP ranges for those endpoints.

Azure workload identity federation setup creates an Entra application/service principal and federated credentials, then stores Azure configuration in GitHub secrets; this is a procedure, not permission to create resources.
Review trust hardening; api://AzureADTokenExchange is the recommended Azure audience, but other values are permitted and require provider-specific review.
Workflow authentication combines OIDC issuance permission and azure/login JWT exchange; environment protection is recommended when environments participate.
The sample root OIDC permission and Azure action reference/client/tenant/subscription placeholders are illustrative; they establish neither safe action origin nor an adopted root-permission policy.
The sample Azure account/group listing demonstrates resource access after login; no real cloud read or access test occurred.
The reusable comment preserves third-party action terms/privacy/support and absence of GitHub certification.
Further-reading links do not certify other source artifacts or the provider configuration.

scope: Full pinned article and literal closure read; source propositions are reference-only and do not adopt policy.
